body:
### Related

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41634

### Problem

How to know whether following mode is enabled to toggle it programmatically?

Take `vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor`, for example. Should it move only the main cursor or all cursors at once (see https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41634)? Both behaviors are useful, but temporarily toggling following mode is easier than trying to follow all cursors programmatically.

### Expected behavior

Maybe:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_get_mode().mcursor_following
```

comment_data.body:
An API is planned, but in general it shouldn't be necessary for plugins to care. If `nvim_win_set_cursor` is called by a mapping, when it cascades per-cursor the mapping acts as if the current cursor is the main cursor, and thus should just work (or there's a bug in multicursor). 

So the details matter, i.e. need a concrete use-case in this report.

A usecase I came across is the need to restore following mode state before/after a keymap.
E.g. I have 2 keymaps currently, that always end with following mode disabled:
`vim.keymap.set("n", "<Up>", "Qk")` and `vim.keymap.set("n", "<Down>", "Qj")`

Ideally I'd like these keymaps to keep the following mode state before/after, but, if I understood correctly, that would currently require me to manually create the mark with `vim.api.nvim_mcursor` manually and then move the cursor in way that won't cascade regardless of following mode(Or maybe the creation prevents cascade anyway?).

In general I think keymaps that create new multicursors could benefit from knowing when following mode is active.

I think most plugins shouldn't need to care about this until it is something like [multicursor.nvim](https://github.com/jake-stewart/multicursor.nvim).

In general, the idea is:

1. Disable "following" mode.
2. Change the cursor.
3. Restore "following" mode (what exactly should be restored?)

This is already how `/` searching works with "following" mode enabled: it only moves the main cursor. A similar use case could be 2d jumping.

I can also imagine [multicursor.nvim](https://github.com/jake-stewart/multicursor.nvim) relying on this, but I'm not sure whether this would be enough for plugins like that.

> A similar use case could be 2d jumping.

jumps in general are not cascaded, so that should already "work".

I assume `vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor` will move all cursors when "following" mode is enabled. If so, plugins like [mini.jump2d](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.jump2d) might want to prevent cascading even when "following" mode is enabled. But to be honest, this is mostly speculation on my part, so I hope some real-world use cases come up.

Technically, multicursor mode can be disabled with `<C-l>` and restored with `gQ`, but by default `gQ` doesn't restore the follow-mode.

P.S. I guess deleting all cursors disables follow-mode automatically.

Actually, I have a use case.

I want to implement sticky cursor, like in the example here:
https://github.com/jake-stewart/multicursor.nvim/wiki/More-examples#sticky-cursor

For the implementation, I need to move the cursor with `api.nvim_win_set_cursor()`. Basically, I need a way to move the main cursor while bypassing follow mode.

> sticky cursor, like in the example here: https://github.com/jake-stewart/multicursor.nvim/wiki/More-examples#sticky-cursor ... I need to move the cursor with `api.nvim_win_set_cursor()`

Not sure what that video is showing, but `nvim_win_set_cursor` in a mapping already cascades, and is repeatable, which is what https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41675 addressed. Would help to see a concrete example (using Nvim 0.13 features, not the multicursor.nvim wiki).


Also for reference it looks like your "sticky cursor" is unrelated to the "sticky cursor" mentioned here:

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/41819

I kinda have the code right from the oven, but it might be a bit confusing since I haven't put much thought into it. The idea is for `` to always extend the cursor, regardless of the current follow mode. The behavior changes depending on the follow mode, but it doesn't actually rely on cursor following, more like I'm building different behavior based on the mode flag. In both modes, the cursor extends in the given direction, but when follow mode is enabled, it prefers to jump&delete the next cursor if there is one (what I call a sticky cursor). ### What https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c40ab4a-6001-4807-bb75-b9a3eb06edcf ### How
Code (see line_add_cursor) ```lua local mc = {} local ns_mcursor = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("nvim.multicursor") ---@alias Cursor vim.Pos ---@alias CursorArg vim.Pos|[integer,integer] ---@alias CursorDir -1|1 ---@param buf? integer local resolve_buf = function(buf) return (not buf or buf == 0) and vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() or buf end ---@param buf integer ---@return Cursor[] mc.get_all = function(buf, start, end_) buf = resolve_buf(buf) start, end_ = start or end_ or 0, end_ or start or -1 local extmarks = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_extmarks(buf, ns_mcursor, start, end_) local to_pos = function(extm) return vim.pos.extmark(extm[1], extm[2], extm[3]) end return vim.tbl_map(to_pos, extmarks) end ---@param buf integer mc.has_cursors = function(buf) buf = resolve_buf(buf) return not vim.tbl_isempty(mc.get_all(buf)) end ---@param pos CursorArg ---@return Cursor local resolve_pos = function(buf, pos) return pos.buf ~= nil and pos or vim.pos.cursor(buf, pos) end ---@param buf integer ---@param pos CursorArg mc.set = function(buf, pos) buf = resolve_buf(buf) pos = resolve_pos(buf, pos) vim.api.nvim_mcursor(buf, pos:to_cursor()) end ---@param buf integer ---@param pos CursorArg mc.del = function(buf, pos) buf = resolve_buf(buf) pos = resolve_pos(buf, pos) local at = { pos:to_extmark() } local extmarks = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_extmarks(buf, ns_mcursor, at, at) for _, extm in ipairs(extmarks) do local id = extm[1] vim.api.nvim_buf_del_extmark(buf, ns_mcursor, id) end end ---@param buf integer mc.clear = function(buf, start, end_) buf = resolve_buf(buf) start, end_ = start or end_ or 0, end_ or start or -1 vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, ns_mcursor, start, end_) end local follow_assumed = false -- Global mc.is_follow = function() return follow_assumed end ---@param enable boolean|1|2|nil mc.toggle_follow = function(enable) if type(enable) == "boolean" then follow_assumed = enable elseif vim.v.count == 1 then follow_assumed = true elseif vim.v.count == 2 then follow_assumed = false else follow_assumed = not follow_assumed end vim.cmd("normal! " .. (follow_assumed and "1q=" or "2q=")) return follow_assumed end mc.call_no_follow = function(cb) local is_follow = mc.is_follow() mc.toggle_follow(false) cb() -- HACK: Remove `vim.schedule` when fixed in Neovim -- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41836 vim.schedule(function() mc.toggle_follow(is_follow) end) end vim.keymap.set("n", "Q", function() follow_assumed = false return "Q" end, { expr = true, desc = "Override `Q`" }) vim.keymap.set("n", "q=", function() local is_follow = mc.toggle_follow(vim.v.count) -- Sync local msg = string.format("q=: %s", is_follow) vim.notify(msg, vim.log.levels.WARN) end, { desc = "Toggle multicursor follow-mode" }) ---@param buf integer ---@param row integer 1-based ---@param dir CursorDir local iter_lines = function(buf, row, dir) return function() if row < 1 or row > vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf) then return end local lnum = row local line = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, row - 1, row, false)[1] row = row + dir return lnum, line end end ---@param dir CursorDir local line_add_cursor = function(dir) return function() local win, buf = 0, 0 local mcursors = mc.get_all(buf) if vim.tbl_isempty(mcursors) then mc.toggle_follow(true) end local main_pos = vim.pos.cursor(win) local next_pos if dir > 0 then next_pos = vim.iter(mcursors):find(function(pos) return pos > main_pos end) else next_pos = vim.iter(mcursors):rev():find(function(pos) return pos < main_pos end) end if next_pos and mc.is_follow() then mc.del(buf, main_pos) mc.del(buf, next_pos) mc.call_no_follow(function() vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(win, next_pos:to_cursor()) end) return end local next_row = main_pos.row + 1 + dir for row, line in iter_lines(buf, next_row, dir) do if #line > main_pos.col then mc.set(buf, main_pos) mc.call_no_follow(function() vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(win, { row, main_pos.col }) end) return end end end end local expand_word = function() local vis_mode = string.match(vim.api.nvim_get_mode().mode, "[vV\22]") local reg = vim.fn.getregion(vim.fn.getpos("."), vim.fn.getpos("v"), { type = vis_mode or "v", }) if vis_mode then return reg[1] else local char = reg[1] local is_keyword = vim.fn.match(char, "\\k") == 0 return is_keyword and vim.fn.expand("") or char end end ---@param word string ---@param dir CursorDir ---@param current? boolean local search_word = function(word, dir, current) vim.fn.setreg("/", word) vim.o.hlsearch = false local flags = "W" .. (current and "c" or "") .. (dir > 0 and "" or "b") vim.fn.searchpos(word, flags) end ---@param dir CursorDir local match_add_cursor = function(dir) return function() local mcursors = mc.get_all(0) if vim.tbl_isempty(mcursors) then mc.toggle_follow(true) end local word = expand_word() mc.call_no_follow(function() -- BUG?: Set only the current search_word(word, dir, true) local cursor = vim.pos.cursor():to_cursor() vim.api.nvim_mcursor(0, cursor) search_word(word, dir) end) end end ---@param dir CursorDir local match_skip_cursor = function(dir) return function() mc.call_no_follow(function() local word = expand_word() search_word(word, dir) end) end end vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", function() local vis_mode = string.match(vim.api.nvim_get_mode().mode, "[vV\22]") if not vis_mode then mc.clear(0) vim.cmd("nohls") end return "" end, { expr = true, desc = "Clear multicursors" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", "[C", { desc = "Go previous cursor" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", "]C", { desc = "Go next cursor" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", line_add_cursor(1), { desc = "Cursor below" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", line_add_cursor(-1), { desc = "Cursor above" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", line_add_cursor(-1), { desc = "Cursor above" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", line_add_cursor(1), { desc = "Cursor below" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", match_add_cursor(1), { desc = "Cursor match next" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", match_add_cursor(-1), { desc = "Cursor match previous" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", match_skip_cursor(1), { desc = "Cursor match next" }) vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "", match_skip_cursor(-1), { desc = "Cursor match previous" }) ```
